F2 Federal Reserve automated-access/rate contract - UNKNOWN (no robots.txt served, no documented ceiling located)
F4 release-line parsing rule and EST/EDT resolution - unspecified; all sampled items fall inside EDT

capture_spec_readiness.note: provider_selected_for_6ga = true and ready_for_capture_spec_freeze = false are both correct simultaneously
remaining: exact feed URL and host allowlist
release-line parsing rule and EST/EDT resolution (F4)
capture_spec_readiness.why_not: Provider selection is now sound, but freezing is a separate gate. Of the minimum contract the design requires, the Fed still lacks: an automated-access/rate policy (F2), revision/change-detection semantics (F1), a release-line parsing and DST resolution rule (F4), a chosen poll cadence, and a frozen host allowlist and endpoint.

design_fit_recheck.DURABLE_OBSERVED: supported - observed_at + commit-bound ingested_at govern live collection safely
design_fit_recheck.RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE: weaker - no trustworthy source publication bound; date-only at best
design_fit_recheck.TimestampTrustPolicyV1: acceptanceDateTime cannot earn public-availability trust; it is not a publication instant
design_fit_recheck.note: design rev4 already permits source_available_at = null with observed_at bounding, so no design change is needed

edge_case_argument.argument: "SEC is preferable because it forces 6G-A to exercise the source_available_at = null path."
edge_case_argument.reasoning: EventStore edge and pathological paths - source_available_at null, late observed_at, failed commit, same-timestamp conflict, revision correction - are testable with deterministic synthetic fixtures. Moreover TimestampTrustPolicyV1 has four verdicts (TRUSTED_EXACT, TRUSTED_CONSERVATIVE, UNTRUSTED, UNKNOWN) and NO single real provider exercises them all, so branch coverage necessarily comes from fixtures, never from provider choice. The rationale therefore belongs to test planning and must not rank providers.
edge_case_argument.where_it_may_still_appear: test planning / synthetic fixture notes only

evidence.source_title: BEA API for Data Retrieval User Guide (April 20, 2026)
evidence.summary: "users must obtain a unique 36-character UserID by registering"; UserID is a minimum parameter on every request. Registration required; disposable e-mail addresses rejected.

evidence.source_title: BEA API User Guide - API Calling Limits
evidence.summary: Three standard limits for all accounts: 100 requests per minute, 100 MB data volume per minute, 30 errors per minute; exceeding any triggers a timeout period of about one minute.
The user guide section reviewed does not document exposure of originally-published vintages versus currently-revised values.
No official BEA market-consensus product was found; expectations would require a separate provider.
GDP Advance / Second / Third Estimate appear as separately scheduled, separately titled release events - naturally representable as append-only distinct events rather than mutations of one value.
Static JSON/XML API responses; byte-for-byte preservation straightforward.
An "Archive" section for past news releases is linked; the depth and per-document permanence were not verified in this pass.
Times such as "8:30 AM" and "10:00 AM" are listed, but NO timezone is stated on the schedule page.

evidence.source_title: BEA API User Guide - Data Return Format
evidence.summary: JSON or XML via the ResultFormat parameter; JSON is the default.
v1.0 is unregistered/keyless; v2.0 "Registration is required" and returns a key by email. Credential friction applies only to v2.0.
v2.0: 500 daily queries, 50 series/query, 20 years/query. v1.0: 25 daily queries, 25 series/query, 10 years/query.
No documentation found on whether the API exposes originally-published vintages or only the current (possibly revised) series. This is the central causal question for macro values.
The FAQ does not document any per-value publication timestamp or release date. Absence of documentation only - NOT evidence it is unsupported.

No official BLS market-consensus product was found. BLS publishes official statistics; market expectations would require a separate, independent provider. Recorded as UNKNOWN rather than NOT_SUPPORTED because absence of evidence is not proof of absence.
Releases carry a USDL identifier (e.g. USDL-26-1191), an agency-assigned document number usable as a deterministic identity component.

evidence.source_title: CPI News Release (news.release/cpi.htm and archived PDFs)
evidence.summary: News release documents carry "Transmission of material in this release is embargoed until 8:30 a.m. (ET)" - explicit time WITH timezone on the primary document, unlike the schedule page.
No documented field or footnote code distinguishing preliminary from revised values was found in the FAQ.
Static HTML and PDF release documents; byte-for-byte preservation straightforward.
Dated archive URLs of the form /news.release/archives/cpi_08122025.pdf preserve each release as originally published, which is the surface that can reconstruct original (unrevised) values.
Schedule lists "Release Time: 08:30 AM" per reference month, but NO timezone is stated on the schedule page itself.
Public pages and feeds; no authentication encountered or documented as required.

A request for /robots.txt returns the site's standard "Page not Found" HTML document rather than a robots file, so no crawl directives are published at that path. No documented request-rate ceiling, User-Agent requirement or automated-access policy was located on official pages in this pass. ABSENCE OF A DECLARED RESTRICTION IS NOT PERMISSION: this stays UNKNOWN and a future CaptureSpec must adopt a conservative self-imposed cadence.
The FOMC calendar page does NOT state release times; the exact time lives on each statement document, not the schedule.

FOMC statements are Board-authored agency material published by the issuing agency itself. This is a materially clearer authorship position than SEC filings, which are THIRD-PARTY FILER submissions that may embed filer-owned or third-party copyrighted exhibits. NO official reuse/licence terms page was verified for federalreserve.gov, so NO redistribution permission is claimed - only that authorship is unambiguous and that the third-party-rights layer present in SEC filings is absent here.

Items are identified by an official feed-declared <guid> (see feed_item_guid) whose value is the canonical document URL, following the stable dated pattern monetary{YYYYMMDD}{a|b}{n} for both page and PDF. Deterministic, stable and parseable. The earlier framing - penalising this as "not an agency-assigned opaque identifier" - is WITHDRAWN as aesthetic rather than evidential: the design requires deterministic identity, not opacity.

evidence.source_title: FRB: Press Release - Monetary Policy (RSS 2.0) — discovery shape
evidence.summary: A single ~9.6 KB official feed enumerates recent monetary-policy releases with title, link, guid, description, category and pubDate per item. For a narrow FOMC-statement V1, DISCOVERY is one fetch of one declared feed and FETCH is one static primary page - no entity index, no per-issuer fan-out, no credential. This is a materially simpler discovery surface than an entity-scoped filing history. Exact endpoint and cadence are NOT frozen here.
The statement page and its PDF carry "For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT" - minute precision WITH an explicit timezone, on the primary document.

Every item in the official monetary-policy feed carries a declared <guid> element. Inspected 15/15 items: guid present on all, value equal to the item <link> (the canonical press-release URL, pattern monetary{YYYYMMDD}{a|b}.htm); no isPermaLink="false" attribute is set. This is an OFFICIAL FEED-DECLARED, stable, deterministic per-item identifier and is sufficient as a SourceObservation identity input. It is NOT an agency-assigned opaque numeric id, but determinism - not opacity - is what the design requires. No stronger GUID semantics (uniqueness guarantees, mutation policy) are claimed than were observed.

evidence.source_title: FRB: Press Release - Monetary Policy (RSS 2.0) — pubDate
evidence.summary: Each item carries an RFC-822 <pubDate> with an explicit timezone, e.g. "Wed, 29 Jul 2026 18:00:00 GMT". On all four FOMC statements present in the feed (2026-03-18, 2026-04-29, 2026-06-17, 2026-07-29) pubDate is 18:00:00 GMT = 14:00 EDT, matching the release line printed on those documents. It is not a hardcoded constant: a non-statement item in the same feed carries 19:00:00 GMT. CAVEAT - the feeds page documents no pubDate semantics, and every sampled item falls inside EDT, so DST handling is unverified. This is therefore recorded as CORROBORATING DISCOVERY/FEED-TIMING EVIDENCE ONLY. The authoritative source-time evidence remains the release line on the primary statement; pubDate is NOT claimed to carry universal exact-publication authority.

The feeds page documents no update frequency and no formal item-timestamp semantics; pubDate is therefore not established as an authoritative publication field BY CONTRACT. Empirical corroboration is recorded separately under feed_pubdate_corroborates_release_time and is not treated as documentation. F3 remains open but NON-BLOCKING: the primary statement carries its own release line, so the feed is needed for discovery, not for source_available_at.
Materials linked from this page span 2021-2027. Deeper historical archives exist elsewhere on the site but their release-time metadata was not verified in this pass.
Official RSS/XML feeds published, including /feeds/press_all.xml and /feeds/press_monetary.xml (monetary policy press releases).
"The minutes of regularly scheduled meetings are released three weeks after the date of the policy decision."

The official feeds page declares 31 RSS/XML feeds, including /feeds/press_monetary.xml whose channel description is "Press releases about monetary policy from the Federal Reserve Board", alongside /feeds/press_all.xml and topic feeds. The monetary-policy feed is thus an OFFICIALLY DECLARED, topic-scoped surface rather than an incidental endpoint.
A separate "Last Update: June 17, 2026" field exists, date-only. Per design section 7 this is site-maintenance metadata and must NOT be treated as publication time.
No official documentation found stating whether released statements can be corrected in place or how corrections would be exposed.
acceptanceDateTime is present on filings.recent and follows ISO-8601 of shape YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ. Observed uniformly across a 400-value sample of one company's filings; no sample rows retained.
Millisecond field representation (.sss). Supersedes the earlier UNKNOWN, which was an environment limitation rather than a documentation gap.

evidence.source_title: Accessing EDGAR Data (SEC) — Business hours and dissemination
evidence.summary: CROSS-SURFACE PROVENANCE CORRECTED. The verbatim field definition "The ACCEPTANCE date and time of the registrant's filing with the Commission. Filings accepted after 5:30pm EST are considered filed on the following business day" is documented for the FINANCIAL STATEMENT DATA SETS field, NOT for the Submissions API field, and is no longer relied on as sole proof for filings.recent.acceptanceDateTime. The acceptance-versus-dissemination distinction for the SELECTED Submissions surface rests instead on EDGAR operational documentation, which separates acceptance from dissemination directly. The field name and the operational rule agree, but the selected-surface semantics are therefore classified conservatively as PARTIALLY_VERIFIED rather than VERIFIED.
Values carry a trailing Z (UTC) in every sampled value.

evidence.source_title: Determine the Status of My Filing
evidence.summary: Acceptance is NOT proven equivalent to dissemination. Submissions transmitted after 5:30 p.m. ET "will not be disseminated by EDGAR until the next business day", so acceptance can precede public availability by hours. Using acceptanceDateTime as source_available_at would create lookahead for those filings.

No official machine-readable field linking an amendment to the filing it amends was verified. Amendment FORM TYPES (10-K/A etc.) are distinguishable, and each submission carries its own accession number, but an explicit parent pointer was not established. prevrpt is not such a pointer.

Amendment form types (10-K/A, 10-Q/A, 8-K/A) exist and each submission receives its own accession number, implying append-only filing lineage rather than in-place mutation. The exact linkage field between an amendment and its original was not confirmed officially.

The documented "typical processing delay of less than a second" describes surface UPDATE latency relative to SEC dissemination. It is guidance, not a service-level guarantee, and it is not a publication timestamp.
"These APIs do not require any authentication or API keys to access." No credential friction.
companyfacts.zip and submissions.zip offered under /Archives/edgar/daily-index/, "recompiled nightly".

evidence.source_title: Accessing EDGAR Data — Business hours and dissemination
evidence.summary: "EDGAR accepts new filer applications, new filings, and changes to filer data each business day, Monday through Friday, from 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., ET... Some filing submissions that begin after 5:30 p.m. ET - or 10:00 p.m. for Ownership forms 3, 4, 5 - will be disseminated the next business day, showing up in the following business day's index." Second independent official corroboration that ACCEPTANCE CAN PRECEDE DISSEMINATION. Note the precise scope: "some" submissions, keyed to when transmission BEGINS, with a form-conditional cutoff. Not generalised further.
Accession number is a unique identifier assigned automatically by EDGAR to an accepted submission; format ##########-YY-SSSSSS (CIK, 2-digit year, 6-digit sequence). Not URL-derived.

"Each entity's current filing history is available at the following URL: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json". The Submissions endpoint is ENTITY/CIK-SCOPED and is NOT in itself a global new-filing event feed. The object carries "at least one year's of filing or to 1,000 (whichever is more) of the most recent filings"; older history is paginated into additional files listed in filings.files[]. DISCOVERY (learning a filing exists) is therefore a separate concern from FETCH, and for a narrow known-issuer universe discovery means polling known CIKs. No global discovery surface is asserted here.

"The submissions API is updated with a typical processing delay of less than a second; the xbrl APIs ... under a minute." JSON "updated throughout the day, in real time, as submissions are disseminated."
"Our current maximum access rate is 10 requests per second", "carefully monitored to preserve equitable access for all users."

evidence.source_title: SEC Financial Statement and Notes Data Sets
evidence.summary: filed/filingDate is "The date of the registrant's filing with the Commission", a DATE (no time). Combined with the post-cutoff rule it is an ASSIGNED business date and can differ from the acceptance date. It is not an exact publication instant; at best it supports date-only conservative semantics.

evidence.source_title: Determine the Status of My Filing
evidence.summary: "Most live submissions that begin transmission after 5:30 p.m. ET ... will receive a filing date of 6:00 a.m. ET the next business day and will not be disseminated by EDGAR until the next business day." Forms 3/4/5/144 and MEF extended to 10:00 p.m. ET same-date dissemination. EDGAR hours 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. ET. filingDate is therefore an ASSIGNED BUSINESS DATE, not a publication instant.
Four JSON APIs named: submissions, companyconcept, companyfacts, frames, under data.sec.gov.

Official SEC-hosted ticker-to-CIK mapping, 10415 entries, records of shape {"cik_str": <int>, "ticker": <str>, "title": <str>}. Deterministic issuer resolution is therefore available from an official surface. Catalogue examples resolved (METADATA ONLY - the 6G-A universe is NOT frozen): AAPL 320193 Apple Inc.; MSFT 789019 MICROSOFT CORP; NVDA 1045810 NVIDIA CORP; QQQ 1067839 INVESCO QQQ TRUST, SERIES 1. Blocker B5 is RESOLVED.

evidence.source_title: Accessing EDGAR Data — Post-acceptance corrections and deletions
evidence.summary: "Filings are sometimes authorized by SEC staff for removal or correction for a variety of reasons at the filer's request... Corrections processed during a given business day will be incorporated in the indexes built that evening. However, removals processed on subsequent business days will not be reflected in any previous daily, feed, or oldload index. The full and quarterly index files are rebuilt weekly." The SEC PUBLIC SURFACE IS THEREFORE NOT STRICTLY IMMUTABLE: a previously retrievable filing can later be corrected or removed. This does not threaten HyprL causality - HyprL raw-first history stays append-only and a later divergent or absent fetch is a NEW observation/revision state, never an overwrite - but a CaptureSpec must define re-observation and change-detection policy rather than assume upstream immutability.

evidence.source_title: Determine the Status of My Filing
evidence.summary: "Most live submissions that begin transmission after 5:30 p.m. ET ... will receive a filing date of 6:00 a.m. ET the next business day and will not be disseminated by EDGAR until the next business day." Forms 3/4/5/144 and certain MEF types are extended to 10:00 p.m. ET same-date dissemination. The rule is form-conditional and is NOT generalised here beyond the quoted scope.

evidence.source_title: SEC Submissions API — filings.recent field inventory
evidence.summary: prevrpt is NOT a filings.recent field. The Submissions surface inventory is exactly: accessionNumber, filingDate, reportDate, acceptanceDateTime, act, form, fileNumber, filmNumber, items, core_type, size, isXBRL, isInlineXBRL, isXBRLNumeric, primaryDocument, primaryDocDescription. prevrpt belongs to the FINANCIAL STATEMENT DATA SETS, a different SEC product. Recorded to prevent cross-surface schema contamination: the prevrpt prohibition is real but applies to that dataset, not to the selected V1 surface.

evidence.source_title: SEC Financial Statement and Notes Data Sets
evidence.summary: prevrpt: "Previous Report - TRUE indicates that the submission information was SUBSEQUENTLY AMENDED prior to the end cutoff date of the data set." Its value depends on events AFTER the filing and on the dataset cutoff, so it is future-aware and retrospective by construction. It is NOT an amendment parent pointer and MUST NOT enter a causal record or feature at the filing's historical timestamp.

No per-filing public-dissemination timestamp was verified on the Submissions surface. Its field inventory is acceptanceDateTime, accessionNumber, act, core_type, fileNumber, filingDate, filmNumber, form, isInlineXBRL, isXBRL, isXBRLNumeric, items, primaryDocDescription, primaryDocument, reportDate, size. This is a statement about the SELECTED surface only, not about all SEC systems.

evidence.source_title: SEC Submissions — INVESCO QQQ TRUST, SERIES 1 (CIK 0001067839)
evidence.summary: QQQ is NOT a normal operating corporation. Official entity metadata: entityType "investment", with sic, sicDescription, category, ownerOrg and stateOfIncorporation all EMPTY, fiscalYearEnd "0930". Its recent form population is investment-company forms - DEFA14A, 497, 485BPOS, NPORT-P, 24F-2NT, N-30B-2, NSAR-U, 497J - not the 8-K/10-K/10-Q population of an operating issuer. Issuer/event semantics are therefore NOT uniform across a mixed equity+ETF universe, and a CaptureSpec may legitimately need a narrower scope.
Static JSON and filing documents served over HTTPS from /Archives/; byte-for-byte preservation is straightforward, no JS rendering required.

Filings are third-party submissions and may embed filer-owned or third-party copyrighted material (exhibits, logos, images). No official statement establishing redistribution rights for filer-submitted content was verified. SEC-produced API metadata, filer content, HyprL normalized metadata and derived aggregates must be treated as distinct rights categories; no blanket public-domain assumption is made.
No explicit redistribution/licence statement was verified in this pass. US federal agency material is commonly public domain, but that was NOT confirmed from an official terms page.
Declared User-Agent required, documented format: "Sample Company Name AdminContact@<sample company domain>.com".

note: Provider property verification against the frozen causal design, revision 3. Rebuilds the RECOMMENDATION layer after independent counter-review R2 found it unsupported: an invalid selection rationale (the source_available_at = null "edge case" benefit) is withdrawn and given zero ranking weight; Fed identity is re-scored on evidence of an official feed GUID; the SEC revision model is downgraded from immutable/append-only because post-acceptance correction and removal are officially documented; discovery is added as an explicit operational axis; and evidence counts, blockers and environment wording are corrected. The recommendation is REVERSED to federal_reserve. The SEC timestamp findings of revision 2 are preserved unchanged. No capture spec is frozen and no provider code exists. Absence of official documentation is recorded as UNKNOWN, never as false.

02_timestamp_quality.note: earliest discriminating criterion, and the gap is categorical rather than marginal: SEC has no verified source publication instant at all
02_timestamp_quality.sec: WEAK - no verified dissemination instant on the selected surface; backfill date-only

03_deterministic_identity.note: real but narrow: EXCELLENT vs GOOD, not EXCELLENT vs BLOCKING

04_revision_semantics.note: a genuine SEC advantage and a genuine Fed risk (F1). But SEC's model is richer and MORE complex, not cleaner, which cuts against it for a first integration.
04_revision_semantics.sec: GOOD - amendments additive AND correction/removal documented

05_raw_capture_simplicity.fed: EXCELLENT - static XML feed + static page, no JS

06_legal_clarity.fed: Board-authored agency material; no reuse-terms page verified, so no permission claimed
06_legal_clarity.note: no legal overclaim on either side; the difference is authorship clarity, not established permission
06_legal_clarity.sec: third-party filer submissions, may embed filer-owned/third-party copyrighted exhibits; redistribution UNKNOWN

08_historical_fixtures.note: material for offline replay fixtures, but 6G-A needs determinism, not volume
08_historical_fixtures.sec: EXCELLENT - nightly bulk zips, /Archives permanent since 1994, large volume

09_relevance.fed: EXCELLENT - macro, relevant to equities and crypto

10_implementation_simplicity.fed: one declared ~9.6 KB feed + one static page, fixed narrow universe
10_implementation_simplicity.sec: entity/CIK map + per-CIK JSON with pagination + /Archives fetch + UA/rate compliance + heterogeneous entity semantics (QQQ is an investment company with a different form population)

ordered_selection_criteria._contract: The original infrastructure-first priority ordering, preserved verbatim and unrenumbered. discovery_quality is NOT inserted into it.
ordered_selection_criteria._method: Priorities, not a lexicographic algorithm. The earliest DISCRIMINATING criterion carries the most weight, but later advantages are weighed for materiality rather than discarded. The final choice may not contradict the ordering without a stated reason.

bea.deterministic_identity: UNKNOWN - no agency-assigned release id verified
bea.revision_model: GDP Advance/Second/Third are distinct scheduled events (append-only friendly)
bea.timestamp_strength: schedule lists 8:30 AM / 10:00 AM with NO timezone on the page

bls.authentication: v1.0 keyless (25 queries/day); v2.0 registration key (500 queries/day)

bls.historical_archive: dated PDF/HTML archives preserve releases as originally published

blocker_classification.F2: STILL_BLOCKING_CAPTURE_SPEC - automated-access/rate contract UNKNOWN; a conservative self-imposed cadence must be chosen and recorded
blocker_classification.F3: NON_BLOCKING - RSS pubDate is not formally proven as universal publication authority, but it is not needed for that: the primary statement carries its own release line, so the feed serves DISCOVERY while source_available_at comes from the document

blocker_classification.F5: NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_MVP - deeper pre-2021 archive depth unverified; a narrow V1 does not depend on it

causal_grade_caps.historical_backfill: B - archived statements carry the same declared release line, so retrospective source bounds are real rather than reconstructed
causal_grade_caps.live_effective_causality: source_available_at from the document release line AND observed_at/ingested_at independently; DURABLE_OBSERVED and RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE both fully populated
causal_grade_caps.live_source_timestamp_axis: A - official/primary, LIVE, strong provenance, exact declared release instant at minute precision (TimestampTrustPolicyV1 trusted_requires is precision <= minute)
causal_grade_caps.retrospective_source_fit: STRONG - this is the axis on which SEC cannot compete

federal_reserve.deterministic_identity: official feed-declared <guid> per item (15/15 inspected), value = canonical document URL following the stable dated pattern monetary{YYYYMMDD}{a|b}{n}. Deterministic and stable; sufficient as a SourceObservation identity input. Not an agency-assigned opaque id - which the design does not require.
federal_reserve.discovery_model: one officially declared topic feed (/feeds/press_monetary.xml, ~9.6 KB) enumerates items with title/link/guid/pubDate/category. Discovery is a single fetch; fetch is one static primary page. No entity index, no per-issuer fan-out, no credential. Exact endpoint and cadence NOT frozen.
federal_reserve.documented_latency: UNKNOWN - the feeds page documents no cadence; unchanged
federal_reserve.historical_archive: statement pages archived and stable; calendar page links 2021-2027 verified, deeper depth unverified
federal_reserve.rate_policy: UNKNOWN - no robots.txt served and no documented rate ceiling located; absence of a declared restriction is NOT permission
federal_reserve.redistribution_position: Board-authored agency material - authorship unambiguous, and the third-party filer-rights layer present in SEC filings is absent. No official reuse/licence terms page verified, so no redistribution permission is claimed.
federal_reserve.revision_model: UNKNOWN - no documented correction semantics; raw hashing plus re-observation can detect change, but the policy is unverified
federal_reserve.timestamp_strength: PRIMARY AND AUTHORITATIVE: the statement document itself carries "For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT" - minute precision WITH explicit timezone, verified on two independent historical statements (2026-06-17, 2026-07-29). CORROBORATING ONLY: the official feed pubDate matches that instant (18:00:00 GMT) on all four FOMC statements in the feed. Under TimestampTrustPolicyV1 the document release line satisfies trusted_requires (TIER_1_OFFICIAL, precision <= minute, known timezone), so source_available_at CAN be populated. observed_at remains independent - the collector may receive later, and a schedule is never an observation.

blocker_classification.B1a: RESOLVED - acceptanceDateTime is ISO-8601 YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ, UTC, millisecond representation. Verified on the surface itself.
blocker_classification.B1b: NON_BLOCKING_WITH_CONSERVATIVE_POLICY - no per-filing dissemination instant on the selected surface; design rev4 permits source_available_at = null with observed_at bounding. It does cap the causal grade.
blocker_classification.B2: NON_BLOCKING_WITH_CONSERVATIVE_POLICY - raw stays LOCAL_RESTRICTED, redistribution_permitted=false by default, release guard applies.
blocker_classification.B3: NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_MVP - each accession is an independent SourceObservation; a CaptureSpec must declare amendment_parent_lineage_available=false rather than invent one.
blocker_classification.B4: STILL_BLOCKING_CAPTURE_SPEC - the discovery mechanism and polling scope are not decided. A future CaptureSpec must choose among official mechanisms (known-CIK polling, an official recent-filings feed/index, or another verified SEC discovery surface). This does NOT make SEC unsuitable.
blocker_classification.B5: RESOLVED - official ticker/CIK mapping exists at www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json.
blocker_classification.B6: STILL_BLOCKING_CAPTURE_SPEC - post-acceptance correction/removal behaviour is documented upstream but V1 change-detection and re-observation policy is unspecified.

blocking_unknowns: B2 redistribution of filer-submitted raw content - UNKNOWN

causal_grade_caps.historical_backfill: D - no historical observed_at, acceptance must not substitute for dissemination, only date-only filingDate remains
causal_grade_caps.live_effective_causality: SAFE via collector observed_at + commit-bound ingested_at under DURABLE_OBSERVED; honest causality, but not a source-declared publication instant, so it does not earn A
causal_grade_caps.live_source_timestamp_axis: E - no verified per-filing publication instant on the selected surface
causal_grade_caps.retrospective_source_fit: WEAK - the RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE gate is source_available_at <= T, which SEC cannot populate live and can only bound date-only in backfill

sec_edgar.deterministic_identity: accession number ##########-YY-SSSSSS, assigned by EDGAR on acceptance
sec_edgar.discovery_model: Submissions endpoint is ENTITY/CIK-SCOPED (data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json) and is not in itself a global new-filing feed; filings.files[] paginates older history. DISCOVERY is therefore separate from FETCH: for a narrow known-issuer universe it means polling known CIKs, resolved through the official ticker/CIK mapping. Other official discovery surfaces exist but none is selected or frozen here.
sec_edgar.documented_latency: submissions API typical processing delay < 1 second; real time as disseminated
sec_edgar.entity_mapping: Official ticker-to-CIK mapping at www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json (10415 entries). Catalogue examples METADATA ONLY, universe NOT frozen: AAPL 320193, MSFT 789019, NVDA 1045810, QQQ 1067839. QQQ entityType is "investment" with an investment-company form population, so issuer/event semantics are not uniform across a mixed universe.
sec_edgar.prevrpt_warning: retrospective/future-aware; forbidden in causal records and features; not an amendment parent pointer
sec_edgar.rate_policy: 10 requests/second, declared User-Agent with contact e-mail
sec_edgar.revision_model: accession provides deterministic filing identity and amendments (10-K/A, 10-Q/A, 8-K/A) are SEPARATE filings with their own accession numbers, so amendment lineage is naturally additive. BUT the SEC also documents post-acceptance CORRECTION and REMOVAL procedures, so the public surface itself is NOT strictly immutable. A provider implementation must preserve each observation/retrieval state rather than assume upstream immutability.

safe_live_policy.no_derived_0600_timestamp: a conservative next-business-day 06:00 ET bound is NOT adopted; its exact domain is not established and V1 does not invent it
safe_live_policy.observed_at: the collector's first successful acquisition of the public resource
safe_live_policy.source_available_at: null / unavailable - never derived from acceptance or filingDate
safe_live_policy.why_this_is_safe: a collector cannot observe a filing before EDGAR disseminates it, so observed_at naturally prevents lookahead. DURABLE_OBSERVED then gates on max(observed_at, ingested_at), which the design explicitly supports when source_available_at is absent.

sec_edgar.timestamp_caution: THREE separate cautions. (1) filingDate is an ASSIGNED business date, not an exact publication instant. (2) acceptanceDateTime is precise (ISO-8601, UTC, ms) but marks ACCEPTANCE, and is NOT proven equivalent to public dissemination; for post-cutoff filings acceptance precedes dissemination by hours. (3) source_available_at must therefore NOT be populated from either field as an exact dissemination instant. When no dissemination timestamp is available, the safe causal boundary is the collector's observed_at.
sec_edgar.upstream_mutability: DOCUMENTED. Staff-authorised removals/corrections can change what the public surface returns for an already-accepted filing. HyprL raw-first history remains append-only and immutable; a later divergent or absent fetch becomes a NEW SourceObservation/Revision state and never overwrites stored historical raw. The detection and re-observation policy is NOT specified here - see blocker B6.

recommendation.confidence_reason: MEDIUM, not HIGH: the Fed wins the evidence comparison clearly, but two Fed properties remain UNKNOWN (F1 revision/correction semantics, F2 automated-access/rate contract) and they must be resolved before any capture spec is frozen. Confidence is about remaining unknowns, not about the ranking.
recommendation.consensus_gap: No official market-consensus product was verified on the evaluated official surfaces. Consensus will require a separate, independently verified provider. This is NOT a 6G-A blocker, whose objective is ingestion and replay, not surprise.

not_first.bea: registration required, no verified release identity, no timezone on the schedule page
not_first.bls: richest macro relevance but API vintage and revision semantics undocumented, no timezone on the schedule page, and the causal surface is the dated release archive - a heavier first integration

sec_advantages_acknowledged: agency-assigned accession identity is stronger than a URL-based feed GUID
richer amendment/revision ecosystem with documented correction and removal procedures, where the Fed is UNKNOWN
far larger deterministic archive and nightly bulk fixtures
an explicit documented access contract (10 requests/second, declared User-Agent), where the Fed is UNKNOWN
much higher event volume for exercising a store at scale
recommendation.selection_reason: Both providers are TIER_1_OFFICIAL primary sources, so criterion 1 ties and the decision falls to criterion 2, timestamp quality - where the gap is categorical, not marginal. The Fed publishes an explicit source release instant on the primary document ("For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT", verified on two statements, corroborated by the official feed), which under TimestampTrustPolicyV1 satisfies trusted_requires and can populate source_available_at. SEC has no verified per-filing publication instant at all. That difference is not cosmetic: RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE is one of the two MANDATORY snapshot modes and its gate is source_available_at <= T, so a SEC-first 6G-A would leave that mode without real source evidence, while the Fed populates both modes. The Fed additionally wins legal clarity (agency-authored rather than third-party filer content), relevance (macro, spanning equities and crypto), and implementation simplicity by a wide margin - one declared ~9.6 KB feed plus one static page, against an entity index, per-CIK pagination and heterogeneous issuer semantics. SEC's three wins are real but none is categorical: identity is EXCELLENT against a GOOD that is still fully deterministic; revision semantics are documented but richer and more complex, which is a burden for a first integration; and the archive advantage is volume, which 6G-A does not need in order to prove ingestion and replay.
recommendation.verdict_vs_previous: REVERSED - revision 2 recommended sec_edgar; that recommendation did not survive independent counter-review
recommendation.why_sec_is_still_the_right_second_provid: SEC remains fully suitable and its research is retained in full. It is the natural 6G-B / second provider: it contributes the strongest deterministic identity, the largest offline fixture corpus, a documented access contract, and the real-world source_available_at = null path - the latter as a consequence of integrating it, never as a reason for choosing it.

safe_sec_v1_semantics_proposal.filing_date: date metadata only, NOT an exact availability gate

scorecard._discovery_quality_note: discovery_quality is an OPERATIONAL SUPPORTING AXIS added after counter-review because CaptureSpec feasibility depends materially on it. It is NOT inserted into the frozen ten-criterion priority ordering; it informs implementation simplicity, live-capture feasibility and CaptureSpec readiness.
scorecard._scale: EXCELLENT | GOOD | ACCEPTABLE | WEAK | UNKNOWN | BLOCKING. implementation_complexity is scored as SIMPLICITY: EXCELLENT = simplest to integrate.

federal_reserve.identity_quality_note: raised ACCEPTABLE -> GOOD on evidence: an official feed-declared <guid> on 15/15 inspected items. The prior penalty for lacking an opaque agency id is withdrawn as aesthetic.
federal_reserve.redistribution_clarity_note: ACCEPTABLE not GOOD/EXCELLENT: authorship is unambiguous and the third-party filer layer is absent, but no official reuse-terms page was verified

sec_edgar.discovery_quality_note: per-CIK polling is workable for a narrow universe and the official ticker/CIK map exists, but discovery requires an entity-index step and no surface is selected yet
sec_edgar.revision_model_note: downgraded EXCELLENT -> GOOD: amendments are additive and documented, but post-acceptance correction/removal is also documented, so the surface is not immutable

snapshot_mode_fit._why_this_is_not_test_coverage: This is source evidence quality for one of the two MANDATORY snapshot modes, not branch coverage. RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE has visibility rule source_available_at <= T and requires an explicit minimum_causal_quality. A provider that can never populate that gate degrades the mode itself.

federal_reserve.RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE: SUPPORTED - declared release instant populates the gate; backfill grade B

sec_edgar.RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE: WEAK - gate null live, date-only (grade D) in backfill
